title: Relevant Experience vs. Total Employment Years
content: When a JD states '5+ years of Python' or '3+ years of FastAPI', this refers to 5+ years of DEMONSTRATED, RELEVANT experience with that specific technology — not total years of employment where the technology was incidentally used. A candidate with 10 total years but only 1 year of active Python usage does NOT meet a '5+ years Python' requirement. Evidence must show sustained, hands-on, professional-level usage of the technology across multiple roles or projects.

title: Seniority-Adjusted Experience Expectations
content: For senior/staff/principal roles, experience requirements should be interpreted as requiring deep, production-level expertise demonstrated through architectural decisions, team leadership, or measurable business impact — not just years of incidental usage. For junior/mid roles, demonstrated project-level experience with a progression trajectory is acceptable.

title: Domain Experience vs. Tool Experience
content: Domain experience (e.g., '5+ years in FinTech') implies not only technical tool usage but familiarity with domain-specific regulatory constraints, business logic, workflows, and terminology. Tool experience (e.g., '5+ years Python') measures technology depth. These are distinct dimensions. A candidate may have high tool experience but low domain experience — both should be evaluated independently.

title: Minimum vs. Preferred Experience Thresholds
content: When a JD specifies a minimum experience requirement (e.g., '3+ years'), this is a hard floor for MUST_HAVE requirements. PREFERRED requirements (e.g., '5+ years preferred') define the ideal bar — candidates below this are not disqualified but should be noted. Never treat PREFERRED experience thresholds as disqualifying criteria.

title: Gap Periods and Career Transitions
content: Employment gaps or career transitions do not automatically reduce relevant experience. Assess the quality and depth of experience within active employment periods. A candidate with 3 years of intensive, production-scale experience in the required technology may outperform one with 7 years of peripheral usage. Focus on demonstrated evidence of proficiency.
